author: GamingBolt
description:
This year's Xbox showcase was nothing short of extraordinary. Tons of new reveals along with release date announcements  for major upcoming games like Halo Campaign Evolved and Gears of War E-Day.

In this video we will look at 15 of the biggest reveals from the showcase that you likely missed.
title: 15 MUST-SEE Xbox Showcase Game Announcements That Quietly Stole the Spotlight

author: GamingBolt
description:
It's not often you tune into a smaller showcase, expecting huge announcements that will surprise you, but for the second year in a row, the Future Games Show has managed to deliver a very exciting game. Amazingly enough, it's another Mass Effect-inspired experience: Archetype Entertainment's Exodus.

Granted, this isn't a new game announcement like last year's The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. If you've been following the developer's various teasers over the past few months, a bit of this probably seemed familiar. But after years of hearing about its ambition, and how it wanted to deliver this role-playing game that measures decisions in hundreds of years, we have to admit: Exodus is coming together very well.
title: Forget Waiting for the Next Mass Effect, Exodus Could Be the Next Big Sci-Fi RPG

author: GamingBolt
description:
Another update is now live for Crimson Desert, and a new developer roadmap outlines some very interesting additions planned for it. While the promises of a more coherent narrative and added DLC are welcome, how they might change the experience has caught our attention this time. 

Crimson Desert has already changed so much, and the latest update has changed it yet again in ways that have made us quite optimistic about everything that’s slated to be added to Pywel over the remainder of this year. It’s intriguing, and it was interesting enough for us to share our thoughts on how this game could be very different following those additions.
title: Crimson Desert Could Be A Drastically Different Game In Six Months

author: GamingBolt
description:
Fatekeeper certainly has potential, and despite how utterly railroaded the traversal can be, the environmental aesthetics really do stand out for their atmosphere and fidelity. For $10, with a 20 percent discount currently available for two weeks, the barrier to entry is certainly very low, and the team seems open to changing its plans for the sake of whatever players enjoy most. 

But even if you're seeking a dungeon crawler with more grounded, methodical combat, it's probably best to wait a while before diving into everything Fatekeeper currently has to offer.
title: Fatekeeper Early Access Review - Huge Potential, Rough Edges
